newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian Bank launches currency futures.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian Bank launches currency futures.

text.p: The Palestine International Bank said on Wednesday it had become the first Palestinian bank to set up currency futures services at its West Bank headquarters.
The bank said the currency futures and options were aimed at serving speculators, importers, businessmen and investors hedging against exchange fluctuations.
"We are the only bank to do this in the Palestinian territories," a bank official quoted the president of PIB's board of directors Issam Abu Issa as saying.
He said the bank introduced the service 10 days ago but gave no details of the expected turnover.
He said banks currently operating in the West Bank and Gaza Strip only offered spot currency trading. Some provide futures instruments via overseas offices abroad.
Palestine International Bank, which opened its central branch in the West Bank town of El-Bireh in May, aims to have 10 branches in the Palestinian territories by the year 2000.
The Palestinian Finance Ministry says there are 18 banks -- mainly Jordanian and Egyptian -- with 73 branches operating in the West Bank and Gaza.
